sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Pasadena, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Pasadena sits in southeastern Harris County, and houses there sell by cash offer, investor purchase or agent listing. The fastest closings happen when the seller has the deed, a mortgage payoff figure and a tax certificate ready before the contract is signed.

What slows a Pasadena sale is usually not the buyer. It is a title problem, an unpaid tax year, a tenant, or heirs who have not agreed. This page covers the local picture, the Harris County tax steps a seller meets, and the situations that call for extra paperwork.

sections.h2: What is Pasadena's background, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Pasadena is an industrial suburb with a farming past. The Handbook of Texas entry, linked from the city's own site, says John H. Burnett of Galveston founded it in 1893 and named it after Pasadena, California. A rail line came through in 1894, and after the 1900 Galveston hurricane the area became a strawberry center for Gulf Coast farmers.

The economy changed in the late 1930s as ship channel industries grew. Pasadena had 3,436 residents in 1940 and 22,483 in 1950, and the city annexed Deepwater, Middle Bayou and Red Bluff. By 1980 it covered 58.6 square miles. Refineries, the Bayport industrial district and the Johnson Space Center in nearby Clear Lake are tied to local jobs.

Pasadena voted to incorporate in 1923, disincorporated in 1924, and voted again in 1928. The residents formed an independent school system in 1899, the first in Harris County, and the Pasadena district absorbed the Genoa and South Houston districts in 1935.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Pasadena house?
sections.html:
Harris County's tax office bills and collects property tax on Pasadena homes, along with the other taxing units that appear on the bill. The Harris Central Appraisal District sets values, and the Comptroller's property tax basics page explains that appraisal districts appraise as of January 1 and do not set rates.

Harris County's FAQ states that taxes are due upon receipt of the statement and should be paid by January 31 of the following year. If you pay before then, no penalty or interest is added. Ask the tax office for a statement of what is owed on your account before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What do Harris County's penalty and payment rules look like?
sections.html:
The table summarizes what the Harris County Tax Office prints on its FAQ page. Check the live page for the current year before relying on a date.

Harris County Tax Office property tax rules from its FAQ
TopicWhat the office prints
Timely paymentDue by January 31 of the following year
Late month-one charge6% penalty and 1% interest for February
Homestead installment plans12 to 36 months available
Plan start for current-year delinquencyFirst business day in February
Referral to a collection law firmAdditional 15% to 20% penalty on the balance
Tax salesHeld by the eight county constables

A seller whose taxes are behind can pay them from closing proceeds, so a delinquency does not by itself block a sale. It does raise the payoff, so ask for a figure dated for your closing day.

sections.h2: How do taxes get handled at a Pasadena closing?
sections.html:
The title company asks for a tax certificate showing what is paid, and any unpaid amount is collected at closing. The Harris County FAQ flags one trap: a closing scheduled between November 15 and January 31 with a mortgage that escrows taxes. In that case you should call your mortgage company as soon as the date is set, so the bill is paid and the certificate is clean.

  • Tell the title company if your lender paid the current-year bill from escrow.
  • Ask for a refund of any escrow balance after the payoff.
  • If you claimed a homestead exemption and then sold, the county asks you to correct the account so the new owner is not stuck with it.

The state calendar adds that a tax lien attaches on January 1, so a buyer cannot get clear title until the year's taxes are paid.

sections.h2: What exemptions and caps should a Pasadena owner check before selling?
sections.html:
Homestead exemptions affect your tax bill and what a buyer inherits. School districts must give a residence homestead exemption of $140,000, and an owner age 65 or older or disabled gets an additional $60,000 school exemption, per the Comptroller exemptions page.

  • The appraised value of a homestead cannot rise more than 10 percent a year.
  • Disabled veterans may have exemptions from $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a full exemption on the homestead.
  • A buyer who takes the home after January 1 may claim the homestead exemption for the rest of the year if you did not hold it.

Pasadena homes inside the city and in the surrounding district can sit in several taxing units, so look at every line on the bill.

sections.h2: What if the Pasadena house is inherited, in foreclosure or rented?
sections.html:
Each situation has a Texas procedure that a buyer or title company will ask about.

  • Inherited. The State Law Library lists probate of a will, muniment of title, a small estate affidavit and an affidavit of heirship. A will generally has to be probated within four years of death.
  • Foreclosure. Sales take place on the first Tuesday of a month, with a notice of sale posted at least 21 days earlier. A sale before that date pays the loan off.
  • Rented. A tenant must receive a written notice to vacate before an eviction case is filed in justice court. A buyer will want the lease and deposit details.

Deeds are filed with the county clerk. The clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 per added page, plus other records fees.

faqs.q: Which county handles taxes for Pasadena, TX?
faqs.a: Harris County. Its tax office bills and collects, and the Harris Central Appraisal District sets the values. Ask the tax office for a payoff and a tax certificate before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay delinquent taxes before I can sell in Pasadena?
faqs.a: No, you can pay them at closing out of your proceeds. The amount grows with penalty and interest, so ask for a figure dated for the closing day.

faqs.q: When is the Harris County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: January 31 of the year after the tax year, according to the county's FAQ. Taxes paid by then carry no penalty or interest.

faqs.q: What happens to my escrow if I sell in winter?
faqs.a: Your mortgage company may have paid the tax bill from escrow. Tell them the closing date as soon as it is set, and ask for any leftover balance after the payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pasadena house with a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes it subject to the lease unless it ends, and an owner who wants the house empty must follow the Texas notice and justice court steps.
